knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Work beyond training or authority is paused and escalated. The supervisor is told before going further, so authority or training can be confirmed. Relying on footwear, or carrying on because others are doing the task, does not make it safe or authorised.
The supervisor is told that the site rule conflicts with safe performance and what the risk is, so the conflict can be resolved. Working around the rule or keeping quiet about it is not acceptable.

Enclosed slip-resistant footwear suited to the floor conditions and task is the correct choice. The lesson requires enclosed footwear, and footwear reduces risk but does not replace barriers, dry routes or controlled work zones. Slippers, sandals and any flat-soled shoe do not meet that requirement.

Relying on footwear alone on a wet walkway, with no barrier or drying, is the unsafe choice. Footwear reduces risk but does not replace barriers, dry routes or controlled work zones, and soles must be inspected and footwear replaced when grip is inadequate.
The lesson says to report site footwear rules that conflict with safe task performance, so the supervisor can resolve the conflict.

practicalCriteria: Checks the site/task requirements before acting
Identifies and applies relevant safety and privacy controls
Communicates professionally and respects authorisation boundaries
Records the outcome and escalates unresolved issues correctly
passRule: All safety-critical criteria must be demonstrated; remediate and reassess any missed criterion.
evidenceRequired: Record of procedure step 5: Manage spills promptly and keep wet floors controlled.
Record of procedure step 7: Report any site footwear rule that conflicts with safe task performance.
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 7 is not done: Report any site footwear rule that conflicts with safe task performance.
